questions.question: According to article 112 of Indian constitution, who shall cause in every financial year a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, the **President** shall cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, in respect of every financial year, a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India.
 
• This statement is commonly known as the **Annual Financial Statement** or the budget.
 
• The budget is a comprehensive statement that includes details on the revenue and expenditure, proposed allocations for different sectors, and the financial performance of the previous year.
 
• The budget is a crucial document for the economic planning and financial management of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• **The Union Budget** is prepared by the **Ministry of Finance** and presented by the Finance Minister in Parliament.
 
• **After the budget is presented, it must be approved by both Houses of Parliament before it can be implemented.**
 
• **The budgetary process includes debates, discussions, and voting on the budget proposals.**

• These articles outline **the structure, powers, and functions of the state executive**, including the **Governor, Council of Ministers, Chief Minister, and other related provisions.**
 
• **Articles 153-167** of the Indian Constitution, which pertain to the state executive, are mentioned in **Part VI** - **The States of the Indian Constitution.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Article 154: **This article establishes the office of the Governor as the constitutional head of the state executive.
 
• **Article 155: **Article 155 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment of the Governor of a state. .
 
• **Article 156: **Article 156 of the Constitution of India deals with the term of office of the Governor:

• **Article 162: **This article deals with the executive powers of the state and the extent of the executive power of the state government.
 
• **Article 163: **It empowers the Governor to exercise executive powers on behalf of the state government and defines the relationship between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

• **Article 166: **This article deals with the conduct of government business and the duties of the Chief Minister and other ministers.

questions.question: Which type of title can be conferred by the state as per Article 18 of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Military and Academic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 18 of the Constitution of India prohibits the state from conferring any titles except those related to Military and Academic distinctions.
 
• This provision is designed to prevent the state from granting any titles that could be seen as creating a class of nobility or honorific titles.
 
• Military titles could include ranks such as General, Colonel, etc., which are essential for the structure and functioning of the armed forces.
 
• Academic titles could include degrees such as Doctor, Professor, etc., which acknowledge educational and scholarly achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 18**

 
 
• Article 18 of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of titles.
 
• It was introduced to prevent the perpetuation of a system of titles and honors that could undermine the principles of equality enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• It states that no title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the state.
 
• It also prohibits citizens of India from accepting any title from any foreign state.
 
 
 
• **Military Titles**
 
 
• Military titles are ranks given to personnel in the armed forces as a part of their professional hierarchy.
 
• These titles signify their position, responsibilities, and authority within the military structure.
 
• Examples include ranks such as General, Major, Captain, Lieutenant, etc.
 
 
 
• **Academic Titles**
 
 
• Academic titles are conferred upon individuals in recognition of their scholarly achievements and contributions to education and research.
 
• These titles include degrees and honors such as Doctor, Professor, PhD, etc.
 
• They are essential for identifying the qualifications and expertise of individuals in academic and research institutions.

questions.question: 'Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections' comes under which Article of Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 46**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 46 of the Indian Constitution mandates the promotion of the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and other weaker sections.
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• Article 46 aims to protect these communities from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
 
• The state is encouraged to take special care to promote their educational and economic development.
 
• It highlights the importance of equal opportunities and upliftment of marginalized communities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• These principles are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSP aims to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They act as guidelines for the central and state governments in India to frame laws and policies.
 
• Though non-justiciable, DPSPs are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST)**
 
 
• These are officially designated groups of historically disadvantaged people in India.
 
• SCs and STs have been provided with certain privileges and reservations in educational institutions and government jobs to promote their development.
 
• The Constitution of India recognizes the need for affirmative action to uplift these communities.
 
 
 
• **Social Justice**
 
 
• Social justice refers to the fair and just relation between the individual and society.
 
• It includes the distribution of wealth, opportunities, and privileges within a society.
 
• The aim is to create a society based on equality and solidarity, where human rights are recognized and protected.
 
 
 
• **Educational and Economic Development**
 
 
• Educational development involves providing access to quality education for all, especially marginalized groups.
 
• Economic development includes measures to improve the economic conditions of weaker sections through employment, entrepreneurship, and financial inclusion.
 
• Both aspects are crucial for the holistic development of individuals and communities.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India says that the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 44 of the Constitution of India is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which aims to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens throughout the territory of India.
 
• The purpose of a Uniform Civil Code is to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing every citizen.
 
• It seeks to provide equal status to all citizens, irrespective of their religion, and aims at national integration.
 
• The implementation of a Uniform Civil Code is considered essential for the protection of vulnerable sections of society including women and religious minorities.
 
• Despite being a part of the Directive Principles, it is not enforceable by any court, but it is fundamental in the governance of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Part of the Directive Principles of State Policy
 
• Outlines India's commitment to global peace and harmony
 
• Mandates the state to:
 
• Promote international peace and security
 
• Maintain just and honorable relations with other nations
 
• Foster respect for international law and treaties
 
• Encourage peaceful resolution of international disputes
 
 
 
• **Article 40: Organization of Village Panchayats**
 
 
• Also a Directive Principle of State Policy
 
• Encourages the state to organize village panchayats to act as units of self-government
 
• Aims to empower rural communities and promote decentralized governance
 
• Seeks to involve people in decision-making processes at the local level
 
 
 
• **Article 42: Provision for Just and Humane Conditions of Work and Maternity Relief**
 
 
• Another Directive Principle of State Policy
 
• Directs the state to ensure just and humane working conditions
 
• Focuses on:
 
• Fair wages
 
• Healthy work environments
 
• Adequate rest periods
 
• Maternity benefits for working women

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that “it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures" ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51A (g)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A (g):**

 
 
• Article 51A (g) of the Indian Constitution is part of the **Fundamental Duties** under **Part IV-A**.
 
• It states that it is the duty of every citizen of India to **protect and improve the natural environment**, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• This duty was added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of environmental conservation and sustainable development.
 
• The inclusion of this duty reflects the constitutional commitment to environmental protection and ecological balance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A (b):**

 
 
• Article 51A (b) is another Fundamental Duty under the Indian Constitution.
 
• It states that it is the duty of every citizen to **cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom**.
 
• This duty encourages citizens to uphold the values of freedom fighters and contribute to the nation's progress.
 
• It aims to instill a sense of patriotism and respect for the sacrifices made during the independence movement.
 
• However, it does not relate to environmental protection or conservation.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A (j):**
 
 
• Article 51A (j) is also a Fundamental Duty under the Indian Constitution.
 
• It states that it is the duty of every citizen to **strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity**.
 
• This duty encourages citizens to work hard and contribute to the nation's development in various fields.
 
• It promotes a culture of excellence and innovation among citizens.
 
• Like Article 51A (b), it does not address environmental issues or conservation.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A (e):**
 
 
• Article 51A (e) is another Fundamental Duty under the Indian Constitution.
 
• It states that it is the duty of every citizen to **promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood** among all people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities.
 
• This duty emphasizes the importance of unity and social cohesion in a diverse country like India.
 
• It aims to foster a sense of belonging and mutual respect among citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution declares that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall be void?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 13 of the Indian Constitution ensures the supremacy of Fundamental Rights by declaring that any law inconsistent with or derogating from Fundamental Rights shall be void.
 
• The term "law" under Article 13 includes ordinances, orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications, customs, or usages having the force of law.
 
• Article 13 applies to both pre-Constitution laws (laws existing before January 26, 1950) and post-Constitution laws.
 
• This Article empowers courts to review legislation and strike down laws that violate Fundamental Rights.
 
• It serves as the cornerstone of judicial review in India, a crucial tool for protecting citizens' rights from unconstitutional actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution and guarantee civil liberties to all citizens.
 
• They include rights like equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the courts, providing a mechanism for citizens to challenge violations.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• Judicial Review refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive orders.
 
• Article 13 is a foundational provision enabling judicial review in India.
 
• It ensures that laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are invalidated, safeguarding citizens' rights.
 
 
 
• **Pre-Constitution and Post-Constitution Laws:**
 
 
• Article 13(1) deals with pre-Constitution laws, declaring them void if inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 13(2) prohibits the state from making laws that infringe on Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Severability:**
 
 
• Under Article 13, if a part of a law violates Fundamental Rights, only that part is declared invalid.
 
• The remaining provisions of the law continue to be enforceable, provided they are separable and do not contradict the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Eclipse:**
 
 
• Pre-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are not entirely void; they are dormant and overshadowed by the Constitution.
 
• If the inconsistency is removed, the law can become operative again.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?

• **Article 142**, gives the Supreme Court the power to pass any order necessary for doing complete justice in any case or matter pending before it.
 
• **Article 145,** deals with the rules of the Supreme Court, including the number of judges required to sit for a case and the quorum for meetings.
